author: Emma Murphy
title: Denver Couple Charged with Criminal Neglect, Theft, and Tampering After Keeping Decomposing Roommate's Body in 'Throuple' Arrangement, Neighbors Say Shocked
text:
In a shocking case that has sent ripples through the Denver metro area, a married couple in Lakewood, Colorado, has been charged with criminal neglect, theft, and tampering with a human body after allegedly living for over 18 months with the decomposing remains of their roommate—a 64-year-old man they claimed to be part of a ‘throuple’ with.
Suzanne Agnew, 57, was arrested alongside her husband after Colorado police last month found the decomposing body of James O’Neill, 64, who she said had been in an ‘intimate’ relationship with the couple The discovery of James O’Neill’s body, hidden beneath a deflated air mattress in the Agnews’ apartment, has raised serious questions about the intersection of personal relationships, legal accountability, and public health.
The story began when James O’Neill’s brother, Robert, grew concerned after losing contact with his 6’4” sibling for years.
According to an affidavit obtained by Law&Crime, Robert requested a wellness check with police, suspecting that something was amiss.
When officers arrived at the Agnews’ residence in Lakewood, James Agnew, 55, initially claimed to be O’Neill, refusing to speak with his brother.
Her husband, James Agnew, has also been charged with theft and tampering with a body; he told police he took into consideration O’Neill’s continued Social Security payments when deciding whether or not to report his death However, after reviewing body camera footage, Robert confirmed that the man before him was not his sibling, prompting a deeper investigation.
Authorities returned to the Agnews’ apartment to serve a search warrant and discovered O’Neill’s body, which had been concealed in the home for months.
Suzanne Agnew, 57, reportedly admitted that her husband and she had been in an ‘intimate’ relationship with O’Neill, who had been sleeping on a mattress adjacent to their bed.
She claimed that O’Neill had been suffering from severe health issues, including drug use, and that she had discovered him dead in December 2023.
The affidavit includes images of a man who appears to be Agnew using O’Neill’s debit card According to the affidavit, Suzanne allegedly told officers that her husband had suggested contacting the police, but she resisted, fearing the loss of O’Neill’s presence in their lives.
She later covered the body with an air mattress after her eight chihuahuas began ‘chewing’ on it, a detail that has sparked both horror and outrage among local residents.
The financial exploitation of O’Neill’s estate has further complicated the case.
Authorities revealed that the couple had spent nearly $17,500 of O’Neill’s money, including funds from his Social Security payments.
James Agnew reportedly considered whether to report O’Neill’s death, weighing the ongoing benefits against the potential consequences.
The deceased man’s accounts were several hundred dollars overdrawn by the time police and O’Neill’s relatives discovered the scheme – with the couple believed to have spent $17,400 This revelation has led to calls for stricter oversight of financial guardianship in cases where individuals are vulnerable to exploitation by those in close proximity.
Adding to the mystery, an investigation uncovered that O’Neill had contacted authorities in the days before the Agnews claim he died, reporting that his roommate was making threats.
This raises the possibility that O’Neill may have been in a state of distress or fear, further complicating the narrative of his death and the subsequent concealment of his remains.
Local law enforcement has emphasized that this case underscores the importance of promptly reporting missing persons and unexplained deaths, as delays can lead to severe public health risks and legal consequences for those involved.
Public health experts have weighed in, noting that the prolonged presence of a decomposing body in a residential setting poses significant risks, including the spread of infectious diseases and exposure to hazardous materials.
Dr.
Emily Carter, a forensic epidemiologist at the University of Colorado, stated that such cases are rare but serve as a stark reminder of the need for community vigilance. ‘When individuals are in situations where they may be isolated or vulnerable, it’s crucial for family members and neighbors to step in,’ she said. ‘This case highlights the importance of accessible resources for those in need and the legal frameworks that protect both the deceased and the public.’
As the Agnews face charges that could result in felony convictions, the community in Lakewood is left grappling with the unsettling reality of how personal relationships can sometimes cross into the realm of criminality.
The case is expected to be a focal point in upcoming legal proceedings, with prosecutors preparing to argue that the couple’s actions constituted a deliberate and prolonged violation of both legal and moral boundaries.
In a chilling case that has stunned local authorities and neighbors alike, James and Suzanne Agnew are now facing multiple charges stemming from the death of their alleged ‘lover,’ James O’Neill.
According to an affidavit obtained by investigators, Suzanne Agnew confirmed she was seated beside James Agnew during a critical phone call that occurred as their relationship with O’Neill began to unravel.
She told police that at the time, she and her husband were contemplating leaving O’Neill’s home due to the increasingly erratic behavior of James Agnew, a detail that has raised questions about the couple’s state of mind and their potential involvement in the events that followed.
The affidavit paints a troubling picture, revealing that Suzanne Agnew categorically denied any knowledge of harm coming to O’Neill during the night of the fateful phone call.
However, the document also states that James Agnew admitted to police that he likely threatened O’Neill at some point, though he could not recall the specifics of those threats.
This admission, coupled with his acknowledgment that O’Neill’s ongoing Social Security payments were a key factor in his decision not to report the death, has cast a shadow over the couple’s actions and motivations.
The affidavit includes disturbing evidence that appears to confirm the couple’s financial exploitation of O’Neill’s estate.
Among the documents are images of a man resembling James Agnew using O’Neill’s debit card at multiple 7-Eleven locations.
According to the affidavit, O’Neill’s account continued to receive $967 monthly Social Security deposits even after his death, with all funds being spent by the Agnews.
By the time authorities and O’Neill’s relatives uncovered the scheme, the account was overdrawn by several hundred dollars, and the couple had allegedly spent $17,400 from the deceased man’s accounts.
Suzanne Agnew reportedly told police that O’Neill’s money was used to pay bills, though the affidavit details other transactions, including payments to Google, Progressive Insurance, and Sally Beauty Supply.
The couple’s actions did not stop there.
Four months after O’Neill’s death, James Agnew applied to be added to the title of O’Neill’s 2008 Ford Expedition, using a forged signature from the deceased man.
The car was eventually towed, left unclaimed, and sent to auction—a move that has further fueled suspicions of the couple’s intent to erase any trace of O’Neill’s existence.
Neighbors of the Agnews at their neatly kept apartment complex have expressed shock at the revelation that O’Neill had been living with the couple.
One elderly woman, who resides just a few doors away, described James Agnew to the Daily Mail as ‘spooky as hell’ and shared that she had hidden valuables in her garage after noticing his unusual interest in her belongings.
This account has added another layer of unease to the already unsettling narrative surrounding the couple’s behavior.
As the legal proceedings unfold, Suzanne Agnew is set to appear in court next week, while her husband is scheduled to face charges in September.
The case has drawn significant attention from law enforcement and the public, with credible expert advisories emphasizing the need for transparency and accountability in such matters.
The Agnews’ alleged exploitation of O’Neill’s estate, combined with the tampering of a deceased human body, has raised serious concerns about their actions and the potential impact on public trust in legal and social systems.
Authorities continue to investigate the full scope of the Agnews’ involvement, with the affidavit serving as a critical piece of evidence in what is being described as a complex and disturbing case of financial and emotional manipulation.
As the story develops, the community and legal system alike are left grappling with the implications of a tragedy that has exposed deep vulnerabilities within a private relationship.
